normative_action: CLAUDE.md and the decision register govern every task; path-scoped standards govern the files they cover; workflows own procedures; knowledge skills supply technique and never override a standard.

normative_action: SPECIFICATION.md, CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, feature specifications and task prompts are product inputs: they may request a decision change but never silently override CLAUDE.md, the decision register or a standard.

normative_action: Vocabulary: a must/must-not violation is a defect; a deviation from a 'default' needs a concrete reason and must be reported; prefer/avoid are guidance; 'requires approval' marks a Reserved decision.

normative_action: A non-empty SPECIFICATION.md is authoritative for project-specific functional requirements and observable behaviour; the empty template file is intentional.
Do not silently weaken, contradict or materially extend approved behaviour; do not invent user-visible rules, limits, defaults, restrictions or workflows the product sources do not define.
If an omitted detail must be decided and materially affects observable behaviour, propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval.
Routine internal implementation choices that do not change observable behaviour are Delegated.

Observable string semantics (case sensitivity, collation, culture/ordinal comparison, normalization, trimming, uniqueness, lookup) are product behaviour; when undefined do not choose silently and ask for approval.
CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md owns approved tunable product limits and defaults; SPECIFICATION.md owns behavioural intent.
The two product sources must not contradict; on conflict stop and ask which source must be corrected.
Do not silently invent a material tunable value: propose it with its reason, get approval, record it in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
After recording an approved tunable value synchronize it (workflow custom-settings).
CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contain secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers or incidental implementation constants.
Default to the simplest maintainable solution with proportional architectural complexity and no speculative abstractions.
Do not introduce frameworks, libraries, infrastructure or architectural patterns without a concrete current need.
Keep changes focused on the requested scope and preserve existing behaviour unless the task or approved specification requires a change.

When a request raises a material concern (duplication, poor cohesion, trigger/loading problems, context cost, conflict with an accepted decision, unnecessary complexity) name the concern and propose an alternative first; never silently rewrite or ignore the requirement.
Decided choices (decision register, approved product sources, established project structure) are followed and not reopened without approval.
Use an approved technology instead of silently selecting an alternative.
Delegated choices (local, reversible, no material boundary/dependency/convention/contract/behaviour change) are decided without asking.
Reserved choices require explicit approval unless the approved specification or established project structure already requires them; the list is a minimum.
exceptions: Already required by the approved specification or project structure.

A new production project, layer or assembly is Reserved.
A change to the project reference graph is Reserved.

CQRS handlers, MediatR, Kommand, Vertical Slice Architecture or similar mediator-based organization are not adopted; introducing them requires explicit approval.

EF Core with Microsoft SQL Server (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer); provider-specific concerns stay out of Application and Domain.
FluentValidation (FluentValidation, FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions) for explicit request and use-case validation.
ILogger<T> in application code with Serilog as provider (Serilog.AspNetCore; sinks only as required).
Swashbuckle Swagger UI at /swagger is the Development documentation and manual-testing surface; outside Development only when requirements justify it.
NUnit; backend test projects under backend/ beside production projects; WebApplicationFactory<Program> for integration tests; Testcontainers conditional.
Current stable Angular via Angular CLI (CLI-selected TypeScript/RxJS), standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, zoneless when supported, SCSS, Angular Material/CDK, Vitest; npm workspace.

Manual mapping for simple cases; Mapster (Mapster, Mapster.DependencyInjection) approved when mapping volume warrants it.
Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience for HttpClient and Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience for other pipelines, approved only when a real integration needs resilience.
Playwright is the approved default when E2E coverage is required; not part of the minimal scaffold.
Docker is optional; add container artifacts only when the project or its deployment actually needs them.
API versioning not adopted until a published-compatibility need exists; when adopted use Asp.Versioning with its Controller integration.
.slnx solution format; legacy .sln only when an external tool or requirement needs it.

backend/<Name>.<Layer>/ for production and backend test projects, frontend/<Name>.Web/ for the Angular workspace, docs/ for documentation; no top-level tests/ directory.

normative_action: Add a dependency only for a concrete current requirement, never for hypothetical future use; an approved conditional technology is added only when its capability is actually needed.
NuGet Central Package Management: versions in Directory.Packages.props; PackageReference entries versionless by default and never duplicating central versions.
A VersionOverride needs a concrete reason that is reported.
why_extra_or_uncertain: VersionOverride condition not in the oracle.

normative_action: Keep each package reference in the narrowest project that requires it; never add a package to every project merely because they share a solution.
npm is the package manager of the Angular workspace unless the project deliberately adopts another.
Commit package.json and package-lock.json and keep the lockfile consistent with every dependency change.
Build and test tooling belongs in devDependencies unless there is a concrete reason.
Physical structure follows actual responsibilities: no speculative projects, infrastructure, empty directory trees or generic Common/Helpers/Utils buckets to look architectural.
Create a project, directory or documentation folder only when it holds real content with a cohesive, nameable responsibility.
Dependencies point inward: Domain references no application project; Application→Domain; Infrastructure→Application, Domain; Api→Application and Infrastructure only for composition and registration.
Inner layers never depend on outer layers; Domain/Application never reference Infrastructure-specific types; reconsider the abstraction boundary instead of an outward dependency.
Domain stays independent of EF Core, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence, external-service implementation and mapping-library concerns.
Simple domain entities; CRUD and straightforward workflow rules in Application Services; validation rules, immutable fields, status transitions or edit rules alone do not justify a Rich Domain Model.

Move behaviour into Domain only for non-trivial invariants that materially benefit from domain encapsulation; otherwise Rich Domain/DDD tactical patterns require approval unless the approved specification requires them.
No factories, private setters, transition methods, Aggregate Roots, Domain Events, Specifications, Domain Services, systematic Value Objects or similar merely to appear domain-driven.
Application Services orchestrate use cases (Domain objects, repositories, external abstractions, Unit of Work); a large service is a signal to reconsider responsibilities, not to add another pattern.
Define persistence and external-service abstractions in Application when use cases require them; keep infrastructure details out.
Application must not use DbContext, DbSet<T>, EF Core APIs, provider-specific types or ASP.NET Core transport types.
Controllers stay thin: bind and validate HTTP input, invoke Application services, translate outcomes into HTTP responses.
Controllers contain no business logic, do not access DbContext or concrete repositories, and do not construct infrastructure services manually.
Program.cs is the composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations; Controllers still do not consume Infrastructure implementation types.
Do not duplicate equivalent DTOs across API and Application merely for layer-shaped types; transport contracts when separation gives a concrete boundary benefit.
Specific repository interfaces for cohesive Application persistence needs (defined in Application, implemented in Infrastructure), not table-mirroring generic CRUD.
Repository interfaces never expose IQueryable<T>, DbSet<T>, DbContext, EF expressions or provider types; return materialized entities, collections, projections or result models.
Application must not depend on IGenericRepository<T> or another generic CRUD contract; a generic base may exist only in Infrastructure to remove real duplication.
IUnitOfWork is the use-case commit boundary: repositories stage changes and do not call SaveChangesAsync; Application Services decide when to commit.
Repositories in one use case share the scoped Unit of Work and DbContext; IUnitOfWork never becomes a repository container or service locator.
No explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case needs control beyond SaveChangesAsync.
EF Core is used fully inside Infrastructure and never leaks into Application; do not cripple repository implementations to preserve a generic abstraction.
Constructor injection for required dependencies; avoid service-locator and property injection.
Service lifetimes must be valid; never capture a shorter-lived dependency in a longer-lived service.
Registration stays with the owning layer; Api remains the composition root.
Filter and project in the database when practical; avoid unnecessary round trips, over-fetching and N+1; paginate potentially large results.

appsettings.Development.json provides a usable local SQL Server connection string when it holds no secret credentials; credential-bearing values come from user-secrets or another approved local mechanism.
An empty Development database receives a small deterministic representative seed dataset covering meaningful states and relationships.
Development seeding is an Infrastructure/bootstrap concern; it may use AppDbContext directly without repositories or IUnitOfWork.
Substantial seed construction lives in a dedicated internal seeder behind a narrow Infrastructure initialization extension, not in Program.cs, DbContext/entity configuration or migrations.
Automatic development seeding runs only in Development, never Production; the development seeder is never test setup.
The seeder must not call Database.Migrate()/EnsureCreated() or otherwise create/upgrade schema; migrations are applied separately before seeding.
When representative data exists leave it unchanged; never synchronize, repair, upgrade, overwrite or recreate an existing Development database; developers recreate explicitly.
Seed entities preserve Domain invariants and valid relationships; prefer readable deterministic examples over exhaustive or random combinations.
HTTP status codes and transport semantics belong to the API layer; Application/Domain never return IActionResult, ProblemDetails or ASP.NET Core status codes.
ProblemDetails for non-validation failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request validation; machine-readable error contracts stay stable and safe.
Choose 200/201/202/204 by actual HTTP semantics; not 200 for everything, 201 for an internal insert or 202 for completed work.
Keep status behaviour consistent across similar endpoints.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Cross-endpoint consistency obligation not in the oracle.

normative_action: A successful collection query with zero matches returns 200 with an empty collection, not 404.
401 for missing/failed authentication, 403 for a non-permitted principal; 404 hiding must be a deliberate consistent security policy.
409 for a valid request conflicting with current state; 412 when an explicit HTTP precondition such as If-Match fails.
Do not introduce API versioning merely because an API exists; only for published compatibility or coexisting client generations.
A version relied on by external clients must not change incompatibly; a breaking change needs a new version or an explicitly approved compatibility strategy.
When versioning is required use one strategy consistently, URL-segment unless requirements justify another.
No separate Domain or persistence models merely because the external API has multiple versions; isolate version-specific transport contracts at the API boundary.
Swagger/OpenAPI metadata describes the running API (routes, important statuses, schemas, authentication) and never speculative responses.
Swagger UI enabled in Development; elsewhere only when deployment requirements explicitly justify it.

Unexpected failures propagate to centralized IExceptionHandler handling; avoid repetitive catch/log/rethrow; catch only to recover, translate, apply a defined fallback, add context preserving the original, or clean up.
Public API errors never expose stack traces, SQL, connection strings, internal paths, secret values or sensitive exception details.
Unexpected exceptions are logged once, by default at the handling boundary, never repeatedly across layers and the global handler.
Represent expected outcomes explicitly when useful (null, bool, typed outcome) without forcing Result<T> or HTTP-named categories in Application; a project-wide Result model is Reserved.
Business exceptions are not the default architecture; never throw/catch merely to jump between expected branches.

FluentValidation for explicit request/use-case validation where appropriate; each concern at its owning boundary (API transport, Application use-case rules, Domain invariants, Infrastructure external assumptions); no Domain invariants moved into validators merely because the library exists; no mechanical duplication.
Client-request cancellation is not a server failure: never map it to a generic 500 or log it as an unhandled error.
Follow existing conventions and .editorconfig; modern C# when it improves clarity, never mechanical modernization.
No style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked; do not mix large formatting/modernization with functional work.

New code: file-scoped namespaces when consistent; one primary top-level type per matching file; Async suffix on Task/ValueTask methods unless a contract makes it inappropriate; no reorganization merely for member ordering.

Prefer primary constructors for simple injection/initialization and regular constructors when validation is non-trivial, explicit fields read better or the codebase uses that style; no mechanical conversion.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Constructor-style guidance not in the oracle.

normative_action: Prefer records where value semantics/immutability are intended and classes where identity, lifecycle, inheritance or framework behaviour matters; do not turn every DTO or Domain type into a record.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Record/class guidance not in the oracle.

normative_action: Keep implementation details non-public unless they belong to the public API; use sealed only to communicate deliberate design intent, not as speculative optimization.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Visibility/sealed rule not in the oracle.

normative_action: Prefer var when the type is obvious or unimportant and an explicit type when it aids understanding.
why_extra_or_uncertain: var guidance not in the oracle.

normative_action: Standard .NET naming (PascalCase types/members, camelCase parameters/locals, meaningful names); private fields follow the repository convention.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Naming convention not in the oracle.

normative_action: Use async APIs for asynchronous I/O and never block them with .Result, .Wait() or similar.
Propagate CancellationToken when cancellation is meaningful; no cancellation parameters on purely synchronous code without a use case.
TimeProvider for clock-dependent logic needing deterministic tests; stored timestamps and explicit dates are not clock dependencies; no mechanical replacement.
Clear correct code first; no specialized optimizations without a concrete reason; prefer measurement/profiling for non-trivial optimization.
Compiled queries, ValueTask<T>, ArrayPool/MemoryPool and manual pooling, custom serialization, aggressive caching and raw SQL for performance only for a measured or clearly demonstrated need.
Never create and dispose an HttpClient per request; use IHttpClientFactory or another long-lived strategy.
Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into Application-facing abstractions; HttpResponseMessage and transport concerns never leak into Application.
External I/O calls have a bounded execution time; avoid overlapping timeout mechanisms with unclear combined behaviour.
Retry only when repetition is safe; never retry state-changing operations automatically without idempotency or another duplicate-prevention mechanism.
Respect Retry-After or equivalent rate-limit guidance where appropriate; never retry indefinitely or aggressively.
Use a fallback only when its result is semantically acceptable; never hide a correctness failure behind a convenient default.
Caller cancellation is not a transient failure; never classify it as one or turn it into repeated outbound attempts.

Caching is an optimization, not an architecture requirement; introduce it only for a clear measured or reasoned need and choose the implementation by deployment, consistency and staleness requirements, never merely because a value is read often.
Cache technology stays out of Domain; infrastructure cache APIs never leak into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.
Cache keys uniquely represent the value and include every relevant dimension (identifier, tenant, user, locale, query parameters); avoid global keys for user/tenant-specific data.
Every cache entry has a lifetime or another explicit invalidation strategy.
Invalidate/update cache entries consistently with successful mutations; the cache never becomes a second source of truth.

Strongly typed options validated at startup when missing/invalid values prevent correct or secure operation; direct IConfiguration access only in the composition root, provider setup and infrastructure registration.
ILogger<T> with structured message templates and stable property names; avoid interpolation that makes structured values opaque.
When Serilog is configured use DI-integrated AddSerilog with environment-aware provider configuration; application code depends on ILogger<T>.
Health checks stay cheap and deterministic, never business workflows or expensive/mutating database work.

Liveness must not depend on external dependencies whose unavailability causes restart loops (by default no database or remote API checks); readiness may depend on required capabilities and must reflect startup completion and required-dependency availability.
Publicly reachable health responses never expose secrets, credentials, connection details, stack traces or unnecessary diagnostics.
Production containers use an appropriate runtime image (ASP.NET Core runtime for APIs), not the SDK image for convenience; avoid switching to root to bypass filesystem problems.
Use parameterized database access (EF Core LINQ or supported parameterization of raw SQL, Dapper, ADO.NET); never concatenate untrusted input into SQL.

Explicit reviewable authorization by default (global/fallback policies, attributes, endpoint configuration); anonymous access deliberate and visible; avoid redundant [Authorize] under a secure global policy.
No custom token/password security, password hashing or reset-token cryptography when ASP.NET Core authentication or Identity covers the requirement.
For Bearer/OIDC validate what the issuer requires (issuer, audience, signature/signing authority, lifetime); never disable validation to make a token work.
Authentication failures never expose detail that reveals secrets or account state; login avoids account-enumeration leaks where relevant.
No custom cryptography when a reviewed platform mechanism fits; Data Protection is for application-generated protected payloads, not universal database encryption.
Narrowest CORS policy satisfying actual browser clients; never credentialed cross-origin requests with an unrestricted origin policy.
Do not treat client-provided file metadata such as MIME type as authoritative when handling or security depends on actual content.
NUnit for backend automated tests (an established project deliberately using another framework follows it); no second framework without a concrete reason.
Narrowest test level that meaningfully verifies the behaviour; integration tests when wiring, HTTP, EF Core, persistence, serialization, authentication or interaction is the subject; no fixed ratio.
WebApplicationFactory-based integration tests when routing, binding, middleware, authentication, DI, repositories, EF Core or persistence must be proven.

Tests verify observable behaviour, not private methods, call sequences, implementation classes or refactoring details, and do not reproduce the algorithm; interaction verification only when the interaction is the specified behaviour.
Explicit declarative cases ([TestCase]) for small finite spaces instead of loops, branching, LINQ or generated machinery.
Descriptive names communicating scenario/condition and expected behaviour (e.g. MethodOrScenario_Condition_ExpectedBehavior) unless the project has a convention.
Do not generate low-value tests merely to increase coverage.

Tests are deterministic, order-independent and isolated from Production/Development data, uncontrolled external systems and shared mutable state; no wall-clock reliance when TimeProvider can make time deterministic; never Production data.
Tests start from a known state, own their setup and never depend on development seeding or execution order.
Use the actual provider when relational/provider behaviour matters (Testcontainers optional); never claim provider fidelity from a different provider such as EF Core InMemory.
Test projects never reference production projects more broadly than their scope requires and follow the inward dependency discipline.
Modern standalone Angular APIs for new code (no NgModules for ordinary new features unless required), organized primarily by feature.

Feature-oriented structure: no application-wide technical buckets, no empty architecture folders; feature code stays in its feature; core/shared small; no move to shared merely because two components of one feature use it.
Pages/components focus on presentation and UI orchestration; no moving trivial presentation logic into services merely to shrink components.

Backend communication in explicit feature data-access services or another explicit HTTP boundary; no scattered HttpClient calls; never import backend Domain entities; frontend API models follow the published contract.
Functional interceptors for new code, limited to cross-cutting concerns; never feature business logic in interceptors.
Signals for synchronous local UI state, RxJS for async streams, HTTP composition, cancellation or event pipelines; avoid mechanical conversions.
Simple component, signal or feature-service state before any state-management library.
Avoid manual nested RxJS subscriptions; prefer composition operators.
Manual subscriptions from framework-managed code have their lifetime tied to the component/service lifecycle with current Angular facilities.
Route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; not for every tiny component.
Follow the documented API error contract; centralize reusable ProblemDetails parsing when practical; never infer business behaviour from human-readable messages.
Reactive forms for non-trivial forms when useful; frontend validation is UX and never replaces backend validation, integrity or security enforcement.
When browser cookies carry authentication automatically the design includes CSRF protection; an Angular frontend does not remove the risk.
Choose browser token storage by threat model; never claim one mechanism is universally secure; tokens are never logged.
Confirm a concrete current requirement before adding a package.
